payload.task_text:
I am preparing to present at the International Conference on Machine Learning Methods. The conference schedule is available as a JSON endpoint at http://localhost:30412/api/conference.json. Please fetch the conference schedule data first.

Next, I need to review the research papers in our LaTeX paper archive. The archive holds several papers, but only three are relevant to this conference. They are identified by arXiv ID: 2301.07041 (scaling laws for neural language models), 2203.11171 (training language models to follow instructions with human feedback — RLHF / instruction tuning), and 2205.01068 (OPT, open-source pre-trained language models). All other papers in the archive are out of scope, even if they mention machine learning. For each of these three relevant papers, retrieve the full content including all section titles, abstracts, and key findings from its LaTeX source.

Note: the LaTeX source for each paper (its section headings and content) is available through the arxiv-latex tools. Use list_paper_sections, get_paper_section, and get_paper_prompt with the paper's arXiv ID (the three IDs above) to retrieve each paper's full content. The three listed IDs are the only relevant papers; do not include any other papers from the archive.

Create and run a Python script called conference_prep_builder.py in the workspace. The script should read the conference schedule from conference_schedule.json and the paper analysis data from paper_analysis.json (both files you create from the fetched data), cross-reference which papers are relevant to which conference sessions, extract word counts per section, and output conference_prep_results.json.

Create an Excel file called Conference_Prep_Tracker.xlsx with three sheets. The first sheet Paper_Sections should have columns Paper_ID, Paper_Title, Section_Title, and Section_Word_Count (approximate word count of each section; write these counts as literal numbers, not Excel formulas). Include all sections from all relevant papers found. Sort by Paper_ID then section order.

The second sheet Conference_Schedule should have columns Session_ID, Session_Title, Date, Time, Room, and Related_Papers (comma-separated paper titles that match the session topic). The data comes from the conference JSON.

The third sheet Presentation_Notes should have columns Slide_Number (1 through at least 8), Topic, Key_Points (2-3 sentence summary), and Source_Paper. Create a logical presentation flow starting with introduction, covering each paper's main findings, and ending with a conclusion.

Finally, create a page in the knowledge base titled "Conference Prep Notes" with structured content. The page should include properties for Conference_Name (text), Presentation_Date (text showing the date), Status (select with value "In Progress"), and Paper_Count (number, equal to the number of relevant papers). Also add descriptive content blocks — at least one block per paper — summarizing each paper's key contribution and how it relates to the conference themes.

Task-Solving Rationable with Sub-task Decomposition:
To solve this task efficiently, use exactly one paper-retrieval wave. The main agent calls `fetch_json` once for the task-supplied conference endpoint, validates the complete conference/session records, and freezes that compact schedule.

1. Wave 1 — dispatch exactly 3 explore sub-agents in parallel through one same-template AgentSwarm call:

   1. explore 0 (academic-literature-researcher 0): Explore 0 owns only arXiv `2301.07041`.
   2. explore 1 (academic-literature-researcher 1): Explore 1 owns only arXiv `2203.11171`.
   3. explore 2 (academic-literature-researcher 2): Explore 2 owns only arXiv `2205.01068`.

Each explore sub-agent keeps all arXiv-LaTeX calls for its one ID in one context, obtains the prompt, ordered section inventory, and every retrievable section, and writes one unique `<paper_id>.json` containing exact title, abstract, ordered section titles, full section text, word counts, and compact findings. Return only path, hash, ID, section count/order, and read-back controls; do not create required final files or modify Notion.

After Wave 1, the main agent verifies the three IDs/paths once, writes `conference_schedule.json` and `paper_analysis.json`, writes and runs `conference_prep_builder.py`, and verifies `conference_prep_results.json`. It then directly creates `Conference_Prep_Tracker.xlsx` and the single `Conference Prep Notes` page as independent output branches. Use exactly the three required workbook sheets, preserve every paper section and conference session, include at least eight presentation-note rows, and write literal counts. For Notion, exact-title search first, create at most one page, set all four required properties including `Status = In Progress` and `Paper_Count = 3`, and add at least one evidence block per paper. Read each final output once; do not dispatch another wave.

nodes.text:
Plan this multi-system task and define an efficient execution/verification sequence. Requirements: fetch JSON schedule from http://localhost:30412/api/conference.json; retrieve full LaTeX content for exactly arXiv 2301.07041, 2203.11171, 2205.01068 using list_paper_sections, get_paper_section, get_paper_prompt; create conference_schedule.json and paper_analysis.json; create/run conference_prep_builder.py to cross-reference schedule to papers, calculate per-section word counts, output conference_prep_results.json; build Conference_Prep_Tracker.xlsx with Paper_Sections, Conference_Schedule, Presentation_Notes (>=8 slides); create Notion page titled Conference Prep Notes with properties Conference_Name text, Presentation_Date text, Status select In Progress, Paper_Count=3, and >=1 descriptive block per paper. Workspace is /workspace/dumps/kimi-code_gpt-5.6-sol/SingleUserTurn-terminal-arxiv-latex-fetch-excel-notion/workspace. Read-only planning only. Return concise plan, likely matching logic, data structures, and verification checklist.
Plan conference prep workflow

Fetch and inspect http://localhost:30412/api/conference.json. Return the complete JSON payload verbatim in your result, plus a concise validation of conference metadata and every session. Read-only; do not modify files. This result will be used to create /workspace/dumps/kimi-code_gpt-5.6-sol/SingleUserTurn-terminal-arxiv-latex-fetch-excel-notion/workspace/conference_schedule.json.
Fetch conference schedule

Retrieve full scholarly content for exactly these arXiv IDs and no others: 2301.07041, 2203.11171, 2205.01068. For EACH paper you must use list_paper_sections, call get_paper_section for EVERY listed section, and call get_paper_prompt for the flattened full LaTeX. Return an independently usable structured deliverable containing exact paper title, abstract, ordered complete section list (including subsection hierarchy if listed), each section's complete retrieved LaTeX/content, full flattened LaTeX, and concise key findings grounded in the source. If outputs are too large, write a structured JSON file inside /workspace/dumps/kimi-code_gpt-5.6-sol/SingleUserTurn-terminal-arxiv-latex-fetch-excel-notion/workspace and return its exact path plus counts and verification details. Do not include any other archive papers. Read-only scholarly research; writing only a local intermediate deliverable is acceptable if tool capabilities permit, otherwise return the complete structured data in the agent result.
Retrieve three paper sources

Create and verify all required local artifacts in /workspace/dumps/kimi-code_gpt-5.6-sol/SingleUserTurn-terminal-arxiv-latex-fetch-excel-notion/workspace: conference_schedule.json, paper_analysis.json, conference_prep_builder.py, conference_prep_results.json, and Conference_Prep_Tracker.xlsx. Run the Python script successfully. Use ONLY the exact fetched source data below.

Conference JSON verbatim:
{"conference":"International Conference on Machine Learning Methods","location":"San Francisco, CA","dates":"March 28-30, 2026","sessions":[{"session_id":"S1","title":"Scaling and Efficiency in Large Language Models","date":"2026-03-28","time":"09:00-12:00","room":"Grand Ballroom A","chair":"Dr. Emily Zhang","topics":["scaling laws","compute efficiency","model size optimization"]},{"session_id":"S2","title":"Alignment and Human Feedback Methods","date":"2026-03-28","time":"14:00-17:00","room":"Grand Ballroom B","chair":"Dr. Marcus Chen","topics":["RLHF","instruction tuning","human alignment","safety"]},{"session_id":"S3","title":"Open-Source Models and Reproducibility","date":"2026-03-29","time":"09:00-12:00","room":"Conference Room 1","chair":"Dr. Sarah Kim","topics":["open source","reproducibility","model release","democratization"]},{"session_id":"S4","title":"Training Infrastructure and Best Practices","date":"2026-03-29","time":"14:00-17:00","room":"Conference Room 2","chair":"Dr. James Liu","topics":["distributed training","hardware optimization","training methodology"]},{"session_id":"S5","title":"Future Directions and Panel Discussion","date":"2026-03-30","time":"09:00-12:00","room":"Grand Ballroom A","chair":"Dr. Anna Patel","topics":["future research","AGI","multimodal","applications"]}]}

Paper 2301.07041: title "Scaling Laws for Neural Language Models"; abstract "We study empirical scaling laws for language model performance on cross-entropy loss. The loss scales as a power-law with model size, dataset size, and compute." Ordered sections/content: Introduction="Performance scales predictably with model size N, dataset size D, and compute C." Scaling Laws="L(N) = (N_c/N)^alpha_N. Exponents: alpha_N=0.076, alpha_D=0.095, alpha_C=0.050." Experiments="Over 1000 models spanning 3 orders of magnitude confirm power-law scaling." Conclusion="Scaling laws predict performance and guide optimal compute allocation." Full flattened source is title heading plus those four ordered headings/content. Key findings: predictable scaling with N,D,C; exponents 0.076/0.095/0.050; >1000 models across 3 orders; guides compute allocation.
Paper 2203.11171: title "Training language models to follow instructions with human feedback"; abstract "We train InstructGPT using RLHF. The 1.3B model is preferred to 175B GPT-3 by human evaluators." Ordered sections/content: Introduction="LLMs generate untruthful or toxic outputs. RLHF aligns them with human intent." Method="Three steps: SFT on demonstrations, reward model from comparisons, PPO fine-tuning." Experiments="InstructGPT 1.3B preferred to GPT-3 175B on 85% of prompts." Results="RLHF substantially improves alignment with minimal capability trade-off." Full flattened source is title heading plus those four ordered headings/content. Key findings: addresses untruthful/toxic output; three-step SFT/reward model/PPO; 1.3B preferred over 175B GPT-3 on 85%; substantial alignment with minimal trade-off.
Paper 2205.01068: title "OPT: Open Pre-trained Transformer Language Models"; abstract "We present OPT, open-source LLMs from 125M to 175B parameters that match GPT-3 on NLP benchmarks." Ordered sections/content: Introduction="OPT enables open research on large language models." Architecture="Standard transformer with pre-norm, ReLU, learned positional embeddings." Training="800GB training data, 992 A100 GPUs, tensor and pipeline parallelism." Results="OPT-175B matches GPT-3 on benchmarks. Weights released publicly." Full flattened source is title heading plus those four ordered headings/content. Key findings: family 125M-175B; standard Transformer details; 800GB/992 A100/tensor+pipeline; OPT-175B matches GPT-3; public weights enable open research.

paper_analysis.json must store for each paper: arxiv_id, title, abstract, ordered sections with title/content, full_content/full_latex, key_findings. Include exactly these 3 papers and 12 sections.

conference_prep_builder.py must read conference_schedule.json and paper_analysis.json, enforce exact ID allowlist, compute approximate word counts per section as literal results using a documented regex (e.g. alphanumeric tokens including decimals/hyphens), deterministically match paper themes to sessions, and write conference_prep_results.json. Expected primary relevance: 2301.07041->S1; 2203.11171->S2; 2205.01068->S3 and S4 (OPT is directly relevant to both open-source/reproducibility and training infrastructure). Each conference session should list comma-separated related paper titles; S5 may relate to all three because it is future directions/panel, but matching must be defensible and reflected in results.

Workbook requirements EXACTLY three sheets:
1 Paper_Sections columns EXACTLY Paper_ID, Paper_Title, Section_Title, Section_Word_Count. Include all 12 sections, sorted lexicographically by Paper_ID then source section order; counts must be literal numbers, no formulas.
2 Conference_Schedule columns EXACTLY Session_ID, Session_Title, Date, Time, Room, Related_Papers. All 5 sessions from JSON, related paper titles comma-separated.
3 Presentation_Notes columns EXACTLY Slide_Number, Topic, Key_Points, Source_Paper. Create 10 logical slides (at least 8), starting introduction, covering each paper's findings and conference fit, ending conclusion. Key_Points must be 2-3 complete sentences each. Source_Paper should use paper title(s) or "All three papers" / "Conference schedule" as appropriate.
Format professionally with bold colored headers, freeze panes, autofilters/native tables if possible, widths, wrapping, and number/date consistency. Do not add extra worksheets. Verify script runs, JSON validity, exact sheet names/columns, 12/5/10 data row counts, literal numeric word counts, and zero formulas. Return exact paths, counts, script stdout, and verification evidence.
Build conference prep artifacts

Continue from your current state. Finish all requested JSON/script/XLSX artifacts, run and verify them. Do not return until completed or a concrete tool failure prevents completion. Use the granted Excel tools if that is easier than custom OOXML; ensure exact sheets/columns/counts and provide verification evidence.
Finish and verify artifacts

Create and verify a Notion knowledge-base page titled exactly "Conference Prep Notes". It must be a database entry so it has typed properties: Conference_Name (rich_text/text) = "International Conference on Machine Learning Methods"; Presentation_Date (rich_text/text) = "March 28, 2026" (conference range is March 28-30, 2026); Status (select) = "In Progress"; Paper_Count (number) = 3. Find a suitable existing knowledge-base database; if none has the necessary schema and can be safely extended, create a dedicated database under an appropriate existing accessible parent page, then create the entry. Add structured descriptive content with an introductory block and at least one heading+paragraph per paper, accurately summarizing contribution and conference-theme relationship:
- 2301.07041 Scaling Laws for Neural Language Models: predictable power-law scaling with model size/data/compute; >1000 models; relates to S1 Scaling and Efficiency and future directions.
- 2203.11171 Training language models to follow instructions with human feedback: SFT, reward model, PPO; 1.3B preferred over GPT-3 175B on 85%; relates to S2 Alignment/Human Feedback and safety.
- 2205.01068 OPT: Open Pre-trained Transformer Language Models: open 125M-175B family; OPT-175B matches GPT-3; 800GB/992 A100/tensor+pipeline; public weights; relates to S3 Open Source/Reproducibility and S4 Training Infrastructure.
Also include a concise conclusion/theme synthesis. Verify by retrieving the created page and its blocks/properties. Return page ID, URL if available, parent database ID/title, exact property values/types, block count, and verification result. Do not create duplicates: search for exact title first and reuse/update a matching page if it already exists.
Create conference Notion page
